meta.title: PrivyMark — Find private details before you share
meta.description: PrivyMark scans your photos on-device for faces, phone numbers, cards, IDs and addresses, and covers them in one tap. Nothing is ever uploaded. Free forever.

hero.sub: A screenshot holds more than you think — a phone number, a card, an address, a face in the background. PrivyMark finds them and covers them in one tap, entirely on your iPhone.
hero.note: iOS 17.6+ · Free forever, no account, no watermark
hero.peek: Hover the block to peek — that's the idea.

trust.title: Private by architecture, not by promise
trust.sub: PrivyMark has no servers, no accounts and no analytics. There is nothing to leak, because nothing leaves.

cards.b: Scanning, covering and exporting all run on your device. Turn on Airplane Mode and everything still works.
No analytics, no ads SDK, no tracking, no crash logs with your content. The privacy label stays minimal because there's nothing to declare.
No history, no copies of your photos. Images handed over from the share sheet are deleted the moment they're read.

features.title: Made for the moment before you hit send
features.sub: From detection to cover styles to metadata, everything serves one flow: share safely.

items.b: Faces, QR codes, emails, phone numbers, URLs, addresses, card-style numbers, ID numbers, order numbers and names.
Solid block (irreversible, the default for text), pixelate, blur — plus a color well to match your style.
Blends a text region into the surrounding background so it simply disappears in place.
Long-press any line to fan it out into word chips — cover exactly the words that matter.
Freehand strokes for anything the scan missed, and a tiled custom watermark for photos you hand out.
Detected faces are covered with an emoji — tap to swap it, drag to reposition. Baked into pixels on export.
See what's inside the file — GPS, device, timestamps. GPS is stripped by default; you choose the rest.
Send a photo to PrivyMark from Photos, Messages or any app, cover it, and share back out.

honest.title: Honest about the limits
honest.body: A privacy tool that overpromises is a privacy risk. So we'll say it plainly:

points.b: Detection is a smart assistant, not a promise. Every match is a suggestion you review — always check before you share.
Pixelation and blur on text can sometimes be undone. That's why text defaults to a solid, irreversible block.
The optional scrub clears simple pixel-level marks and all metadata. It cannot remove robust forensic watermarking.

free.title: Free. Actually free.
free.sub: No subscription, no paywalled tools, no export badge, no account. Covering one photo safely should never be a premium feature.

family.sub: PrivyMark keeps things on your device. These two put you in charge of your own infrastructure.

sections.p: PrivyMark collects nothing. Your photos are processed entirely on your device, are never uploaded anywhere, and we keep no copies. The app has no account system, no analytics, no ads and no tracking of any kind.

Scanning, redaction and export all run locally using Apple's on-device frameworks (Vision, Core Image, and on capable devices Apple's on-device foundation models). Photos never leave your device through PrivyMark. If a photo you pick is stored only in iCloud, iOS downloads it to your device through Apple's own system — it does not pass through any server of ours; we don't operate any.

PrivyMark detects faces only to draw a box around them so you can cover them. It uses Apple's on-device Vision framework, which returns nothing more than the rectangle a face occupies in the image. PrivyMark does not create, use, or store a faceprint, face template, or any other biometric identifier, and it cannot recognise or identify who a person is. Those rectangles exist only in memory while the photo is open in the editor and are discarded when you close it — nothing about a face is written to disk, included in an exported image, shared with any third party, or transmitted off your device. Because none of it is stored or sent anywhere, the retention period is the length of that one editing session.

sections.h: On-device AI, no third-party AI services
sections.p: On devices that support it, PrivyMark makes an extra pass over the text found in your photo using Apple's on-device foundation model (Apple Intelligence), to catch names and ID numbers the pattern rules miss. That model runs entirely on your device. PrivyMark does not use Private Cloud Compute, and it does not send your photos, the text found in them, or any other personal data to OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, or any other third-party AI service, cloud service, or server. The app has no backend of its own.

PrivyMark asks for photo library access only to show your photo grid and to save results; Limited access is fully supported, and you can also use the app without any access via the built-in sample image. The app does not use the camera, microphone, or location.

When you export, PrivyMark strips GPS location by default and lets you decide about other metadata (device model, timestamps, and so on). The optional hidden-mark scrub additionally clears pixel low-bits and removes all metadata from the exported file.
PrivyMark contains no analytics, no advertising SDKs and no third-party tracking of any kind. It sends no telemetry. There are no crash reports containing your images or recognized text.

PrivyMark keeps no history and no copies of your images. Photos handed to PrivyMark through the share sheet are stored briefly in the app's private container and deleted immediately after they are read.
PrivyMark does not collect personal information from anyone, including children.
If this policy changes, the updated version will be posted on this page with a new date. Since the app collects nothing, changes are expected to be rare and editorial.
By downloading or using PrivyMark, you agree to these terms. If you do not agree, please do not use the app.
PrivyMark is a free iOS app that scans photos on-device for potentially private details and helps you cover them before sharing. All features are free; there are no purchases or subscriptions.

Detection is best-effort assistance, not a guarantee. PrivyMark may miss private details or flag things that aren't private. You are responsible for reviewing every image before sharing it. Note that pixelation and blur applied to text can in some cases be reversed — the solid block style is the safe default — and the hidden-watermark scrub cannot remove robust forensic watermarking.
You may not use PrivyMark for unlawful purposes. You are responsible for the images you edit and share and for respecting the rights of people who appear in them.

support.title: Support
support.sub: Answers to the most common questions. Still stuck? Email us — a human reads every message.

faq.a: No. Scanning, covering and exporting all happen on your device. PrivyMark works in Airplane Mode — try it.

faq.q: The scan missed something. What do I do?
faq.a: Long-press the line of text to explode it into word chips and cover exactly what you need, drag a box around any region, or use the Marker to paint over it freehand.

faq.q: It covered something that isn't private.
faq.a: Tap any cover on the canvas to toggle it off, or open the risk list to review every suggestion by type.
It can detect and clear simple pixel-level (LSB) marks and strips all metadata on export. It cannot detect or remove robust forensic watermarks designed to survive edits — no tool honestly can.
Detection rules cover English, Chinese, Spanish, Portuguese, French, German and Italian. On iOS 26+ the system's document reader extends coverage further.

faq.q: Why does export ask to delete the original?
faq.a: Only if you choose “Share & Delete Original” or “Save (Overwrite Original)”. The safe default — “Save a Copy” — never touches your original photo.

support.contactBody: Email appstore@hz.do and include your iOS version and, if possible, a description of the photo type (not the photo itself — we don't want your private images).
